title: Boost Your Brainpower: Exercise Tips for Ambitious Leaders
author: Heather McGonigal
summary: In the third part of her self-care series for leaders, coach Heather McGonigal argues that exercise is one of the first commitments to be sacrificed when work and family expand, precisely because it feels movable. She reframes movement not as fitness but as recalibration, a way to restore energy, clarity, and resilience and to step out of the mental noise of the day. Her key claim is that the best routine is not the most intense one but the one you will actually return to. She also makes a case about thinking itself: answers often surface when leaders stop forcing them and step away from the desk. McGonigal is careful to say this is not another productivity hack but a recognition that people function better when they move and recover. The piece ends with a concrete invitation to schedule one protected block of enjoyable movement this week and to notice its effect on mood, energy, and the quality of thinking.

quotes: Work expands. Our family needs attention. There are errands, obligations, deadlines, and unexpected problems. And because exercise can feel movable, it is often one of the first things to get pushed aside.
Movement is not just about fitness. It is one of the ways we support our energy, our mental clarity, our resilience, and our ability to handle stress.
That is an important distinction, because the best exercise routine is not necessarily the most intense one or the one everyone else is doing.
What matters is finding something that feels supportive enough that it becomes part of your life instead of another obligation you are constantly trying to force yourself to complete.
We tend to believe that the answer will come if we just think harder, stay at the desk longer, or keep staring at the problem.
That does not mean exercise is secretly another productivity hack. It means that human beings function better when we give ourselves opportunities to move, recover, and change our state.
You may discover that taking time away from everything else was exactly what helped you return to it with more of yourself available.
